clue.text: One in field with knee near ground?

definitions.text: One in field with knee near ground?

parts.words: One in field with knee near ground?
parts.note: reads as a person whose stumpy legs bring the knee close to the ground, but is a cricket fielder stationed close in on the leg side

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone in a field whose knees almost touch the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, short leg is a close fielding position near the batter on the leg side; the question mark flags the pun on someone with short legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder crouching close to the batter in that position is one in the field, and stubby legs put knees near the ground.

clue.text: Cleric beheaded in due course

indicators.note: beheaded tells us to remove the first letter of the cleric word

parts.note: a canon is a cleric attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A churchman will lose his head in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for soon or presently, which is what happens in due course.

clue.text: The vest from the west

definitions.meaning: a light, thin garment such as a sports vest or singlet
in poetry a ... is the gentle west wind, the breeze blowing from the west

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme of 'vest' and 'west' disguises two unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Zephyrus was the Greek west wind, and the word also names a fine lightweight vest or jersey.

clue.text: Have I the ability to speak to the masses?

indicators.note: to speak signals that the question is to be heard as spoken words rather than read

parts.note: asking whether I have the ability is asking 'can I?'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are able to address the common people.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with its French pronunciation the word sounds like 'can I?', the question the clue asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaille is a contemptuous French borrowing for the rabble or common people, the masses.

clue.text: Dull fellow with tree that's queen under ground

parts.note: a proser is a tedious person who talks or writes at dreary length
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A boring man with a tree is somehow linked to a buried queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Proserpine (Persephone) was carried off by Pluto to rule the underworld as his consort.
explanation.definitionFit: Proserpine, the Roman Persephone, was queen of the underworld beside Pluto, so a monarch below ground.

clue.text: Imposing on 22 across's time?

definitions.meaning: the eighth month is named for the emperor Augustus, a Caesar, so it is the time belonging to the clue at 22 across

explanation.walkthrough: 22 across is CAESAR; the month was renamed in honour of Augustus Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means dignified and majestic, and the month takes its name from the Roman emperor Augustus.

clue.text: Home student in game could be a wonder

indicators.note: in tells us the home and student letters go inside the game

parts.note: chess is a board game
in means at home
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student at home playing a game might turn out to be a prodigy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinless wonder' is a British jibe for a feeble upper-class twit, so this adjective is the word that could precede 'wonder'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom chinless wonder names a weak, foolish aristocrat, so this adjective is what could make a wonder.

clue.text: Corrupt nobleman from abroad in diocese

indicators.note: in places the foreign nobleman inside the diocese word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A foreign aristocrat is a corrupting influence within a bishop's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to lead astray or corrupt someone morally.

clue.text: A Zionist group's weapon

parts.note: the Irgun was a militant Zionist group in British Mandate Palestine

explanation.surface: A Jewish militant organisation's firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: An airgun is a gun firing pellets by compressed air, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Refuse good looker's wave

parts.note: bran is the husk sifted from flour, regarded as refuse
a dish is an attractive person, a good looker; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Turning down an attractive person's wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to turn down, but it is the noun meaning waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon is to wave or flourish it threateningly.

clue.text: Funny business with a cheeseboard: "_______________________ , Would he have 20 22 across?"(2)

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters that follow are put in a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd enterprise involving a cheeseboard, plus a quotation with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BUSINESS and A CHEESEBOARD fills the blank before 'Would he have murdered Caesar?', since in Shakespeare Caesar wants fat men about him and distrusts lean Cassius.
explanation.definitionFit: In Julius Caesar the lean Cassius leads the plot; the comic question is whether a fatter conspirator would have killed the emperor, so the clause completes it.

clue.text: Parasites in some respectable heads causing division

indicators.note: in places the parasites inside the letters picked out
heads means take the first letter of each of the words some and respectable

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Lice in the heads of decent people cause a split.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture of head lice is false: 'heads' is the selection signal for the initials of 'some respectable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slicer is something that cuts things into pieces, so a thing causing division.

clue.text: Business-speak needs sound inside to harmonise

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: inside puts the sound word within the speaking word

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
a din is a loud noise or sound

explanation.surface: Corporate jargon needs some noise to make things work together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business-speak' looks like one idea, but the hyphen joins two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate things is to bring them into harmony so they work smoothly together.

clue.text: It's in the sticks — make haste

indicators.note: in places the word it inside the sticks

parts.note: celery comes in sticks
it, with the 's as a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone stuck out in the country is urged to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sticks' suggests the remote countryside; here they are sticks of celery. 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or speed, which is haste.

clue.text: Bird, facetious alternative to 24 down

definitions.meaning: a game bird of the moors
24 down is a bird whose name is also a shouted warning to get down; joking, one might shout the name of a different game bird instead

explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is DUCK; the second definition is a joke on swapping one bird for another in the warning cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a moorland game bird, and jokily its name could replace the other bird in a warning shout.

clue.text: Middle Easterner in his element in dance

indicators.note: in puts the Middle Easterner inside his element

parts.note: the desert sand is regarded as the Arab's natural element
an Arab is a person from the Middle East

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern man is in his element when he is dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In his element' reads as an idiom for being happy; the element is literally sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Bones made of 12

indicators.note: made of means the letters of the referenced answer are rebuilt into a new word

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is the word for a cutter that causes division

explanation.surface: Bones produced from a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are the preserved bones or remains of a saint.

clue.text: That must be Gloria, last work of Byrd, they say

definitions.meaning: split as ..., the surname of the film star Gloria plus her initial, so it must be her

definitions.text: last work of Byrd, they say
definitions.meaning: Byrd sounds like bird, and the last song of a bird, the swan, names a final work

explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Renaissance composer of masses with Glorias; 'they say' points to the sound of his name, a bird, the swan, which legend says sings once before dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend that the swan sings only at death gives the idiom for any artist's final work.

clue.text: Inventor sees game end the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the end-of-game words are read backwards

parts.note: no side is the call that ends a rugby match

explanation.surface: An inventor watches the end of a match go badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees' is a link. In rugby the referee calls 'no side' to end the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Backing instrument, a broken reed, played very badly

indicators.note: backing means the instrument is read from the back

parts.note: a drum is a percussion instrument

indicators.note: broken means the letters of reed are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A backing band's instrument with a cracked reed was played terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing instrument' looks like accompaniment; 'Backing' reverses DRUM to MURD, and 'broken' turns REED into ERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang says a performer murdered a piece of music when they played it atrociously.

clue.text: Any use playing with crowned head?

indicators.note: playing means the letters of any use are toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: Is it any use toying with a royal person?
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry IV: 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation says a crowned head lies anxious and troubled, so a king is fittingly described as restless.

clue.text: Told to get hold of a salad

indicators.note: told signals that the phrase is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to seize a is to get hold of a thing

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grab a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'seize a' sounds just like the name of the salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar salad is romaine with croutons, parmesan and a dressing.

clue.text: I must also say, breaking heart and body

indicators.note: breaking means the postscript bursts into the heart word

parts.note: the core is the heart of something
PS, a postscript, is what one adds when one must also say something

explanation.surface: An afterthought breaks someone's heart and body.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dead human being's lifeless remains are its body, as in finding a body at a crime scene.

clue.text: See 11
See 10
Get down from here?

parts.note: get down means crouch to avoid something, and the soft feathers called down come from this waterbird

explanation.definitionFit: To dodge by crouching is to get down, and eiderdown is taken from this bird.

clue.text: Tree, not from the east, in town with stress, so to speak

definitions.text: town with stress, so to speak

parts.note: an ash is a tree

indicators.note: from the east means read right to left, the reverse of the usual westward reading in an across entry

explanation.surface: A tree, not imported from the east, stands in a stressed town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ashton-under-Lyne is a town near Manchester; being under a line, as with underlining, is putting stress on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlining stresses a word, so Ashton-under-Lyne is jokingly a town with stress.

clue.text: In one variation, runner-up docked in front of spacecraft

indicators.note: In puts the shortened runner-up inside the rearranged one
variation means the letters of one are altered in order
docked means the tail letter is cut off, as a dog's tail is docked

parts.note: the runner-up comes second

explanation.surface: In one version, the second-placed finisher was cut short before a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one variation' reads as a version of something, and 'runner-up docked' as a boat; the cut-down second place sits inside the jumbled one.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose cone is the pointed front section of a rocket or spacecraft.
